gen-gf-oxanium-gf-geom: Commanding Oxanium draws every stroke as if with a rounded rod, one weight from start to finish. Geom follows with a lofty lowercase on a plain sans frame, so a long stretch of text feels friendly and easy to move through.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-hammersmith-one: Hammersmith One has rounded strokes like cut lengths of cord, with capitals barely taller than the lowercase around them. And Oxanium above it is the sharper voice, tall in the lowercase and drawn with one uninterrupted line.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-inder: Inder barely separates its capitals from its lowercase. Oxanium above it keeps a constant stroke with no sparkle, so the heading feels engineered while the text underneath stays level and businesslike.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-jaldi: Jaldi pushes its x-height well above the usual and leaves a visibly gaping c, which makes its text feel brushed and friendly. Oxanium looks drawn with a ruler and compass.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Oxanium's monoline stroke, with no swing between thick and thin, gives the headings a machined, uninterrupted look. Kdam Thmor Pro answers by filling the line with big bowls.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-krona-one: Heavy, spread-out and built like iron. Oxanium has no pinched joints or flared ends, and yet Krona One sets lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals, loosely spaced.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-magra: Oxanium holds one unshaded line, with no swing from thick to thin, and its tall lowercase looks large on the page. Magra's lowercase feels just as big-bodied.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-major-mono-display: Oxanium has a high x-height and curves that end in clear daylight, drawn in a single monoline stroke. Major Mono Display glows like neon glass beneath it.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-martian-mono: Martian Mono lays out fixed-width, code-style letters with generous openings in every curve, spaced far apart. But Oxanium's tall, uninterrupted monoline headings are what make this pair distinct.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-matemasie: Matemasie keeps broad gaps between glyphs and only small entry points into its round letters, so its sans is closed where Oxanium is open. Text would settle into an unhurried rhythm.
